subject: geography

moments.title: Silent Spring published
moments.who: Rachel Carson, marine biologist and writer
moments.body: 27 September 1962: 'Silent Spring' is published, exposing the ecological damage caused by synthetic pesticides — especially DDT — bioaccumulating up the food chain. Carson had begun the research in 1957 after letters from a friend whose songbirds had died after aerial spraying.

quote.text: Over increasingly large areas of the United States, spring now comes unheralded by the return of the birds, and the early mornings are strangely silent where once they were filled with the beauty of bird song.

moments.takeaway: The chemical industry mounted a counter-attack — calling Carson 'hysterical' and a 'fanatic'. She defended her work despite terminal breast cancer.

moments.title: From book to ban
moments.body: JFK convened a President's Science Advisory Committee to investigate; its 1963 report largely vindicated Carson. The Environmental Protection Agency was established in 1970. The US banned agricultural use of DDT in 1972.
moments.takeaway: Single books rarely change policy. Silent Spring is a rare exception — a popular book that triggered a regulatory and institutional shift in under a decade.

now.title: Environmentalism's founding text
now.body:
Carson died in April 1964, aged 56. Silent Spring is widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement — the term 'environmentalist' in its modern sense largely dates from this period. Earth Day was first observed in April 1970.

DDT is still used for malaria vector control under WHO guidance — a contested compromise between ecological harm and disease prevention.
now.open_questions: Has the malaria-DDT counterargument unfairly diminished Carson's reputation? Defenders argue she never called for a total ban and that the chemical industry funded anti-Carson revisionism for decades.

reflection: A single book can crystallise a movement that was already gathering. Silent Spring named what people had been observing, used science to validate it, and gave the modern environmental movement a founding text.
